subject: Per-segment cost & latency drilldown + alert tile request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Per-segment cost & latency drilldown + alert tile request

Hey team,

Following up on last week's customer sync with Acme Retail (Kelly Thompson) — they asked for a lightweight way in Console to: 1) inspect cost/latency breakdown for a single tenant but segmented by route/category, and 2) get a tiled alert when a segment exceeds a configurable cost or tail-latency threshold.

High-level ask (MVP):
- A per-tenant "segment drill": select tenant -> show top 10 segments by spend and p50/p95 latency, with quick links to traces.
- A small dashboard tile (1x1) that can be added to an org/tenant home page with: segment name, 24h spend delta, p95 latency, and a red/amber/green state tied to thresholds. Clicking the tile goes to the drill view.
- Lightweight alerting: simple threshold + cooldown, routed to the tenant's owners (email/webhook). No fancy anomaly detection for MVP.

Why this matters: Acme wants to onboard a new payments product but needs visibility per customer segment to decide whether to enable caching/quantization. They will judge Console readiness for expansion on this feature.

Questions for product/observability:
- Marcus: is there existing instrumentation that can return segment-level token counts and per-token cost for a tenant over a sliding 24h window?
- Jasmine: what UX constraints do we have for a 1x1 tile (data latency SLA, acceptable data aggregation windows)?
- Aditya: any concerns on backend compute/cost for generating these per-tenant segment rollups at scale?

I've attached a small sample export from Acme showing their top 6 segments (segment-sample.csv) and a crude mockup of the tile (alerts-tile-mockup.png).

Can we triage and determine whether this fits in Observability Q4 work, or should we scope as a small cross-team spike first? Ideally a short sync early next week.

Thanks,
Naomi
---
Naomi Feldman
Senior Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Per-segment cost & latency drilldown + alert tile request

On Fri, Nov 10, 2028 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Following up on last week's customer sync with Acme Retail (Kelly Thompson) — they asked for a lightweight way in Console to: 1) inspect cost/latency breakdown for a single tenant but segmented by route/category, and 2) get a tiled alert when a segment exceeds a configurable cost or tail-latency threshold.
>
Thanks Naomi — this is a clear ask. Quick answers while I look into instrumentation details:

- We currently emit per-request metadata that includes route id and token counts to the event pipeline. We do not persist per-segment aggregates by tenant long-term; those are computed on the fly for most dashboards.
- Computing true p95/p99 on the fly for the top N segments is doable for tenants with modest QPS but will be expensive for high-volume tenants; we can approximate using histograms we keep for the last 72h.
- Cost attribution per-token exists in the billing path, but tying it to segments requires joining telemetry streams and billing events (we have a near-real-time join in the analytics stack). That join is currently a best-effort job (2-5 min delay).

Proposed MVP technical approach:
1) Use the event pipeline to compute segment rollups every 5 minutes and persist a 72h window in the observability store (pre-aggregation reduces compute when rendering the tile).
2) For p95 we serve value from compressed histograms; for high-volume tenants we show a sampled p95 with a "sampled" badge.
3) Alerting uses the same rollups; keep cooldowns and simple thresholds initially.

I'll open OBS-412 with detailed telemetry questions and an estimated cost delta. If we go this route, we need to estimate storage/compute on the store side — Aditya, can you give ballpark on monthly cost per active tenant for 5-min rollups?

-marcus

Attachment: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kelly Thompson <kelly@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Nov 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Per-segment cost & latency drilldown + alert tile request

Thanks Marcus — that plan sounds reasonable. A couple of clarifications and constraints from Acme (copied Kelly):
- They need p95 accuracy +-10% for decisioning (they won't act on sampled estimates unless flagged).
- Tile needs to update at least every 15 minutes during business hours; 5-minute rollups are fine if served with caching.
- Alerting: they want two canned thresholds (cost spike and p95 breach) and a manual "acknowledge" flow (email + webhook).

I attached the sample CSV exported from their analytics to show segment naming and expected cardinality (segment-sample.csv). Also attached a quick PNG with the tile mockup (alerts-tile-mockup.png) showing the click-through behavior we mentioned.

If we can meet p95 accuracy for the top 10 segments and expose a simple tile + alerting DSL, Acme is likely to sign a pilot addendum. Not asking for long retention in MVP — 72 hours for rollups is acceptable.

Next step: Jasmine, can you and Marcus propose a minimal UX and API contract (inputs/outputs, what the tile API returns) so we can validate with Kelly? I can coordinate a short design review with Acme if needed.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments: segment-sample.csv (CSV, 12 KB); alerts-tile-mockup.png (image, 84 KB)

Ack — thanks Naomi. I've created a short spec draft and linked OBS-412.

Planned next steps:
- Jasmine to produce a 1-page UX/API proposal (what the tile returns, error/empty states, sample payloads) by Mon 11/20. Google doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A_seg-drill-proposal
- Marcus to provide telemetry cost estimate and confirm whether the 5-min rollups + compressed histogram approach meets p95 +-10% for top-10 segments. Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/OBS-412
- Aditya to flag infra limits / storage concerns and suggest an ops guardrail (circuit-breaker for very high cardinality tenants).
- Naomi to coordinate a 30-minute sync with Kelly (Acme) once the UX/API doc is ready — target the week of 11/27.

I'll schedule a 30m slot and share invites once the doc is in a reviewable state. For now marking this as Observability-Q4 candidate and tagging the ticket.

-Jasmine
